svg.title: An everyday change goes from an issue to a released version: An issue becomes a merge request, and the main branch releases the change
svg.text: An everyday change goes from an issue to a released
Scenario: An issue becomes a merge request, and the main branch releases the change
The change rides a merge request

g.text: Given an installed project with the framework already on its main branch
GitLab's page for the main branch of a project the installer already set up. The table lists the framework's files and
folders, among them .agents, .claude/skills, .config, .gitlab-ci.yml, Taskfile.yml and VERSION, all on the commit
"chore: scaffold the project from the devsecops toolbox". There is no README.md yet.
The project's name shows as "project", and dates and avatars are hidden, so the picture is the same on every run.
When the developer opens an issue and creates its merge request, assigned to themself
The developer opened issue #1, "Mention the toolbox in the README", then created its merge request the way the issue's
"Create merge request" button does: the branch is named after the issue, and the description says "Closes #1".
On the right, the developer is the Assignee, and "Work items" lists the issue under "Closing". Nothing is written yet:
the tabs read Commits 0 and Changes 0, and GitLab says "Merge request contains no changes".
When the developer writes a one-line README on the issue's branch, commits it as a
conventional feat and pushes it
The developer's clone of the project, in a terminal. Three typed lines: switch to the issue's branch, write a README of
one line, then add it, commit it as "feat: mention the toolbox in the readme" and push it.
Git answers "create mode 100644 README.md", so the file is new, and "Your branch is up to date", so GitLab has the
commit. The "feat:" prefix follows Conventional Commits, the format the release reads later to pick the next version.

text.tspan: git switch 1-mention-the-toolbox-in-the-readme && echo "This project was scaffolded with The DevSecOps Toolbox."
> README.md && git add README.md && git commit -m "feat: mention the toolbox in the readme" && git push -q && git

g.text: Then the merge request shows that one-line change
The merge request's Changes tab, the page a reviewer reads. The tabs now read Commits 1, Pipelines 1 and Changes 1. The
only file is README.md, a new one, and its one line shows in green, as an addition.
When the merge request's pipeline passes and the developer merges it into the main branch
The same merge request, merged. "Merge request pipeline passed": its nine icons are the nine stages of the pipeline the
project inherited, from plan to feedback, and every job in them passed. Then "Merged by Lambda User", "Deleted the
source branch." and "Closed #1 (closed)".
The last box, "Pipeline passed" on main, is the main branch's own pipeline. The merge moved the main branch to the
developer's commit, and that pipeline ran on it.
Then the release job on the main branch moves the version from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0
The release job of that pipeline on the main branch, on its own page. In its log, Commitizen reads the feat commit:
"increment detected: MINOR", "build: bump version 0.1.0 → 0.2.0", "tag to create: 0.2.0".
The job then opens push access for a moment, pushes the tag ("[new tag] 0.2.0 -> 0.2.0") and the version commit, locks
the main branch again ("push=No one") and ends on "Job succeeded". Nobody asked for a release: every pipeline of the
main branch includes this job.
And the release commit is tagged 0.2.0 and moves VERSION, the Commitizen config and the
CHANGELOG to 0.2.0
GitLab's page for the release commit, "build: bump version 0.1.0 → 0.2.0", the newest on the main branch. The row "Tags"
shows 0.2.0, plain, with no "v" in front.
The commit changes three files. The Commitizen config .config/commitizen/cz.yaml records version 0.2.0 (Commitizen
rewrites the whole file as it saves it, so two other lines change too). CHANGELOG.md gains a 0.2.0 entry listing
"mention the toolbox in the readme", its date hidden so the picture is the same on every run. VERSION goes from 0.1.0 to
